title: CFD-002: the longer run, and the next question.
summary: The extension to approximately 1.50 simulated seconds completes normally. A lower pitch peak adds useful evidence, while the moving mean and unfinished heave rebound leave stability and damping unresolved.
heroAlt: Accepted heave and absolute pitch histories through approximately 1.50 simulated seconds, showing the new extrema and unfinished heave rebound.
heroCaption: 29,908 accepted saved samples, no smoothing. Gold markers identify interpolated extrema; the dashed line marks the previous interval endpoint. 20 km/h · free heave + pitch · surge-constrained · no rider / no jet thrust.

sections.title: The extension is complete
sections.text: The authorized extension completed normally at approximately τ = 1.50 s, with exit code 0 and a normal end in the solver log. All four ranks exited, and the final checkpoint contained the required motion state, moving-mesh points and flow fields. The extension took approximately 53.6 hours of computing time. Simulated time and computing time describe different things.

sections.title: Three new motion turning points
sections.text: Following the completed first interval, the accepted history confirms a new pitch minimum near 9.241° bow-up, a heave minimum near +68.551 mm and a later pitch maximum near 11.616°. Heave then rises to +95.910 mm at the endpoint, with positive vertical velocity; that final position is not a confirmed maximum. Positive heave is displacement from release, and pitch is absolute bow-up attitude.

table.caption: New confirmed extrema · interpolated estimates and saved-step brackets

sections.title: A lower pitch peak is encouraging evidence, not a damping verdict
sections.text: The new pitch peak is approximately 0.979° below the preceding 12.595° peak. The latest trough-to-peak rebound is about 2.374°, compared with 2.569° previously, giving a descriptive excursion ratio of 0.9243. The peak-to-peak interval is approximately 0.641 s. These comparisons are useful, but the mean attitude is moving and the heave rebound is unfinished. A lower peak or smaller rebound alone does not establish modal damping or settled longitudinal stability.

sections.title: The averages still depend on the window
sections.text: The extension’s time-weighted mean is approximately +82.49 mm heave and 10.51° bow-up, while the latest window averages +88.14 mm and 11.36°. The table shows means ± time-weighted standard deviations. These are transient statistics, not equilibrium trim or final resistance figures. Moment is positive bow-up; board weight is 178.518339 N.

table.caption: Transient time-weighted means ± standard deviations · windows end at the actual final sample

sections.title: What the longer trajectory establishes
sections.text: The analysis retains provisional classification D: still migrating toward another equilibrium. Coupled heave/pitch oscillation is evident, but the record does not establish a stable attitude, a persistent limit cycle or sustained growing porpoising. At completion the hull is still rising at approximately +0.03567 m/s while rotating bow-down at approximately −4.992°/s. The two motions have not both settled.

sections.title: The same model, with a longer accepted record
sections.text: The review uses 29,908 synchronized accepted samples across five bounded segments, excluding 813 samples from the abandoned original branch. The extension retains the hull, mesh, mass, centre of gravity, inertia and sixDoF configuration; all 31 protected configuration hashes and the authorized control dictionary matched. Turning points are interpolated within saved brackets and confirmed with five consecutive saved samples on each side. The 20 km/h condition remains free heave and free pitch, surge-constrained, with no rider and no jet thrust. Normal completion does not establish mesh/time-step convergence or physical validation.

sections.title: Keep H0 and resolve the next question
sections.text: The reviewed recommendation is to retain H0 as a provisional comparison baseline. There is not enough evidence to choose a specific Rhino geometry correction. Further CFD-002 time to τ = 2.50 s is recommended to assess whether the mean and amplitude settle, but requires separate approval. No further run or CFD-003 was launched by the completion review. The earlier interval and interim journal entries remain available as the development history.
